claim: There are over a million unique antibodies that are commercially available.
source: In keeping with their importance there are over a million unique antibodies that are commercially available (Dr. Matt Baker, ThermoFisher, personal communication).
evidence: Supported by personal communication from Dr. Matt Baker at ThermoFisher

claim: The largest public antibody initiative has generated greater than 24,000 antibodies corresponding to almost 17,000 human genes.
source: The largest public antibody initiative has generated greater than 24,000 antibodies corresponding to almost 17,000 human genes, with a focus on polyclonal antibodies (Uhlén et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Uhlén et al., 2015

claim: Up to 90% of a select group of 53 landmark preclinical studies suffered from flaws related to ill-defined antibodies.
source: Ill-defined antibodies contribute significantly to a lack of reproducibility in important research efforts including preclinical studies, with estimates that up to 90% of a select group of 53 landmark preclinical studies suffered from such flaws (Bradbury and Plückthun, 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Bradbury and Plückthun, 2015

claim: Five separate validation criteria for antibodies have been proposed by an international working group.
source: One of the groups (Uhlen et al., 2016) proposed five separate validation criteria: (1) genetic strategies in which the specificity of the antibody toward the endogenous protein is confirmed by the loss of signal in cells or tissues comparing parental to knockout (KO) or knockdown controls; (2) orthogonal strategies in which correlations are made between the antibody signal and known information regarding protein abundance or localization; (3) the ability of two independent uncharacterized antibodies recognizing different epitopes in the same target protein to recognize the same protein; (4) using overexpressed epitope-tagged proteins comparing antibodies against the tag to the uncharacterized antibody; (5) immunoprecipitation followed by mass spectrometry to determine if the protein of interest is a major signal in the sample.
evidence: Supported by citation to Uhlen et al., 2016

claim: The C9ORF72 mutation underlies 11.7% of familial FTD cases and 23.5% of familial ALS cases in a North American cohort.
source: In a North America cohort, this mutation underlies 11.7% and 23.5% of familial FTD and ALS cases, respectively, and in a large Finnish population, the C9ORF72 mutation underlies 46.0% of familial ALS and 21.1% of sporadic ALS (DeJesus-Hernandez et al., 2011; Renton et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to DeJesus-Hernandez et al., 2011 and Renton et al., 2011

claim: The C9ORF72 mutation underlies 46.0% of familial ALS and 21.1% of sporadic ALS in a large Finnish population.
source: In a North America cohort, this mutation underlies 11.7% and 23.5% of familial FTD and ALS cases, respectively, and in a large Finnish population, the C9ORF72 mutation underlies 46.0% of familial ALS and 21.1% of sporadic ALS (DeJesus-Hernandez et al., 2011; Renton et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to DeJesus-Hernandez et al., 2011 and Renton et al., 2011

claim: The C9ORF72 mutation is the most common genetic abnormality in both FTD and ALS.
source: Thus, the C9ORF72 mutation is the most common genetic abnormality in both FTD and ALS.
evidence: Inferred from the prevalence data cited in the previous sentences

claim: The literature regarding C9ORF72 subcellular and tissue-distribution is conflicting.
source: It is vital to understand the cell biological role of C9ORF72, but the literature regarding C9ORF72 subcellular and tissue-distribution is conflicting (Burk and Pasterkamp, 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Burk and Pasterkamp, 2019

claim: The lack of consensus on C9ORF72 expression, function and subcellular localization stems in part from the use of non-specific antibodies.
source: We believe the lack of consensus on C9ORF72 expression, function and subcellular localization stems in part from the use of non-specific antibodies.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors based on their findings

claim: HEK-293 cells express C9ORF72 at the 65th percentile according to PaxDb.
source: C9ORF72 is expressed at relatively low levels in most tissues and cell lines ranging from the 77th percentile for HeLa cells to the 35th percentile in RKO cells. We eventually chose to start with HEK-293 cells (expression levels at the 65th percentile) as they are the 5th most abundant C9ORF72 expressing cell line, and are easy to grow and to edit with CRISPR/Cas9.
evidence: Based on data from PaxDb database

claim: CRISPR/Cas9 was used to generate C9ORF72 heterozygous and knockout HEK-293 cells.
source: We then used CRISPR/Cas9 to generate C9ORF72 heterozygous and KO HEK-293 cells.
evidence: Experimental procedure described in the manuscript

claim: More than 100 commercial antibodies for C9ORF72 were initially identified.
source: We initially identified more than 100 antibodies for C9ORF72.
evidence: Based on the authors' search of commercial antibodies

claim: 14 distinct commercial C9ORF72 antibodies were purchased after eliminating redundancies.
source: This led to 14 distinct commercial C9ORF72 antibodies, 10 rabbit polyclonal antibodies, three mouse monoclonal antibodies and one rabbit monoclonal antibody (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Based on the authors' antibody purchasing strategy

claim: Two sheep polyclonal antibodies from the MRC were identified in addition to the 14 commercial antibodies.
source: In addition we identified two sheep polyclonal antibodies from the Protein Phosphorylation and Ubiquitylation Unit of the Medical Research Council (MRC) in Dundee Scotland (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Based on the authors' antibody identification

claim: GeneTex mouse monoclonal antibody GTX634482 demonstrates a strong signal in parental HEK-293 cell lysates that is reduced by ~50% in the heterozygous line and absent in KO lines.
source: This antibody demonstrates a strong signal in parental HEK-293 cell lysates, the signal is reduced by ~50% in the heterozygous line, and no signal for the antibody is detected in the two KO lines (Figure 2).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunoblot data shown in Figure 2

claim: GTX634482 shows no bands other than C9ORF72, even upon long exposure.
source: Moreover, no band other than C9ORF72 is visible, even upon long exposure (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunoblot data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A

claim: Abcam rabbit monoclonal antibody ab221137 and GeneTex mouse monoclonal antibody GTX632041 gave specific signals on immunoblot but showed other non-specific bands upon longer exposure.
source: Abcam rabbit monoclonal antibody (ab221137) and GeneTex mouse monoclonal antibody (GTX632041) also gave specific signals on immunoblot (Figure 2) but other non-specific bands were detected upon longer exposure (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunoblot data shown in Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A

claim: GTX634482 and ab221137 showed strong specific signals in mouse brain extract from wild-type compared to C9ORF72 KO animals.
source: We screened all 16 antibodies using brain extract from wild-type (WT) and C9ORF72 KO animals and found that both GTX634482 and ab221137 showed strong specific signals (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunoblot data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, B

claim: Some antibodies that did not detect C9ORF72 specifically in human lysates could identify C9ORF72 in mouse samples.
source: We were surprised to observe that some antibodies that did not detect C9ORF72 specifically in human lysates could identify C9ORF72 in mouse samples. These antibodies are GTX119776, ab227555 and sc-138763.
evidence: Based on immunoblot comparisons between human and mouse samples

claim: Nine out of 16 antibodies immunoprecipitate endogenous C9ORF72.
source: Of the 16 antibodies, nine immunoprecipitate endogenous C9ORF72, with GeneTex monoclonal antibody GTX632041 demonstrating the most robust enrichment of the protein compared to starting material (SM) (Figure 3A/B).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3A/B

claim: GTX632041 demonstrates the most robust enrichment of C9ORF72 in immunoprecipitation compared to starting material.
source: Of the 16 antibodies, nine immunoprecipitate endogenous C9ORF72, with GeneTex monoclonal antibody GTX632041 demonstrating the most robust enrichment of the protein compared to starting material (SM) (Figure 3A/B).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3A/B

claim: GTX634482 and ab221137 showed no appreciable C9ORF72 immunoprecipitation despite being effective for immunoblot.
source: Seven antibodies showed no appreciable C9ORF72 immunoprecipitation including GTX634482 and ab221137 (Figure 3A/B), which were the most effective antibodies in immunoblot.
evidence: Demonstrated by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3A/B

claim: Approximately 70% of endogenous C9ORF72 is captured from 1 mg of HEK-293 lysates using 1 µg of GTX632041.
source: Approximately 70% of endogenous C9ORF72 is captured from 1 mg of HEK-293 lysates using 1 µg of GTX632041, whereas the other 15 antibodies capture either no protein or at most 20% of total C9ORF72 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Demonstrated by quantitative immunoblot data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1

claim: Mass spectrometry of immunoprecipitates from parental cells identified C9ORF72 and two known C9ORF72-binding partners, SMCR8 and WDR41.
source: Mass spectrometry of immunoprecipitates from the parental cells identified C9ORF72 (13, 24, 19 peptides) and two known C9ORF72-binding partners, SMCR8 (51, 69, 62 peptides) and WDR41 (23, 28, 24 peptides) (Figure 3D, Supplementary file 2) (Sellier et al., 2016; Amick et al., 2016; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: Demonstrated by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 3D and Supplementary file 2, with known binding partners confirmed by citations

claim: The presence of C9ORF72, SMCR8, and WDR41 at near 1:1:1 level indicates that GTX632041 is selective for C9ORF72.
source: The presence of C9ORF72 and its known-binding partners at near 1:1:1 level (when adjusting for the mass of the proteins) indicates that GTX632041 is selective for C9ORF72 and further supports the use of HEK-293 cells in our analysis.
evidence: Based on mass spectrometry data analysis

claim: MMS19 was identified as a novel C9ORF72-binding partner.
source: Interestingly, we also identified MMS19, a 113 kDa protein component of the iron-sulfur protein assembly complex in the immunoprecipitates from parental cells (5, 1, 2 peptides) with no peptides in immuoprecipitates from the KO cells (Figure 3D), suggesting that MMS19 is a novel C9ORF72-binding partner.
evidence: Based on mass spectrometry data showing MMS19 peptides only in parental cell immunoprecipitates

claim: Clathrin heavy chain (CLH1) was identified in immunoprecipitates but with similar numbers of peptides in both parental and KO samples, indicating it is not biologically significant.
source: We also identified clathrin heavy chain (CLH1) with (85, 72 and 58 peptides) but similar numbers of peptides (75, 51, 53) were seen in the KO immunoprecipitations. This clearly indicates that the presence of clathrin heavy chain is not biologically significant but it is not possible to determine if it immunoprecipitates because it cross-reacts with the C9ORF72 antibody or for other non-specific reasons.
evidence: Based on mass spectrometry data showing similar peptide counts in parental and KO samples

claim: All 16 C9ORF72 antibodies gave various staining patterns with no reduction in fluorescent staining in KO cells when HEK-293 cells were fixed in paraformaldehyde.
source: The antibodies gave various staining patterns with no reduction in fluorescent staining in KO cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1

claim: Similar results were seen when HEK-293 cells were fixed in −20°C methanol.
source: Similar results were seen when the cells were fixed in −20°C methanol (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2

claim: U2OS cells have the highest levels of C9ORF72 among the cell lines tested.
source: Of the cell lines tested, U2OS has the highest levels of C9ORF72 whereas RKO cells have lower expression than HeLa (Figure 4—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: Demonstrated by quantitative immunoblot data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3A

claim: The levels of C9ORF72 in motor neurons is similar to that in HEK-293.
source: Interesting, the levels of C9ORF72 in motor neurons is similar to that in HEK-293.
evidence: Based on quantitative immunoblot comparison

claim: GTX632041 is the sole antibody to recognize endogenous C9ORF72 specifically in immunofluorescence analysis of U2OS cells.
source: We screened all 16 C9ORF72 antibodies using this strategy and we found GTX632041 as the sole antibody to recognize endogenous C9ORF72 specifically (Figure 4A/B).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4A/B

claim: GTX632041 immunofluorescence labeling reveals a cytosolic/punctate fluorescence signal that is dramatically reduced in KO cells.
source: Indeed, GTX632041 immunofluorescence labeling reveals a cytosolic/punctate fluorescence signal that is dramatically reduced in KO cells to a level comparable to buffer control (Figure 4A).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4A

claim: GTX634482 shows a punctate and/or neuritic-like signal in specific brain regions of WT mice that is nearly completely ablated in KO mice.
source: A punctate and/or neuritic-like signal is observed in the neuropil of the glomerular layer of the olfactory bulb, the ventral pallidum of the basal ganglia, the CA4 (hilus), CA3, and CA2 region of the hippocampus, the substantia nigra, the inferior olive, and granular layer of the cerebellar cortex of WT mice (Figure 5A, arrows). The signal is nearly completely ablated in the KO mice although there is some non-specific signal seen in the dentate gyrus/CA4, inferior olive and cerebellar cortex sections (Figure 5A, arrows).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 5A

claim: GTX632041 specifically recognizes C9ORF72 in mouse brain sections including those through the hippocampus but staining is not as strong or consistently specific as seen with GTX634482.
source: GTX632041, which is the most effective antibody for immunoprecipitation (Figure 3A) and immunofluorescence (Figure 4A) analysis, also specifically recognizes C9ORF72 in mouse brain sections including those through the hippocampus (Figure 5B) but staining is not as strong or consistently specific as seen with GTX634482.
evidence: Demonstrated by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 5B

claim: Antibody ab221137 did not reveal any signal in the immunohistochemistry analysis.
source: Antibody ab221137, which worked well for immunoblot (Figure 2; Figure 2—figure supplement 1A) did not reveal any signal in the IHC analysis (Figure 5C).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 5C

claim: Endogenous C9ORF72 has been localized to the nucleus by previous studies.
source: Endogenous C9ORF72 has been localized to the nucleus (Renton et al., 2011; Atkinson et al., 2016), early endosomes (Farg et al., 2014; Shi et al., 2018), recycling and late endosomes (Farg et al., 2014), the Golgi apparatus (Aoki et al., 2017), stress granules (Chitiprolu et al., 2018) the cytoplasm, neurites, growth cones (Atkinson et al., 2016), and lysosomes (Shi et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple previous studies

claim: Each of the previous studies on C9ORF72 localization performed immunofluorescence using commercial C9ORF72 antibodies that failed the validation criteria in this study.
source: Each of these studies performed immunofluorescence using commercial C9ORF72 antibodies that failed our validation criteria.
evidence: Based on the authors' validation results compared to antibodies used in previous studies

claim: A previous study using CRISPR to add an HA tag to endogenous C9ORF72 revealed a diffuse cytoplasmic localization under basal conditions and concentration on lysosomes following starvation.
source: One study used CRISPR to add an HA tag to endogenous C9ORF72, localizing the fusion protein with an antibody against the tag. This study revealed a diffuse cytoplasmic localization for tagged C9ORF72 under basal cell culture conditions, with the observation that the protein became concentrated on lysosomes following starvation (Amick et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Amick et al., 2016

claim: C9ORF72 demonstrates a consistent lysosomal localization under basal conditions.
source: Under basal conditions, C9ORF72 demonstrates a consistent lysosomal localization (Figure 6A, top panels).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6A

claim: Starvation leads to larger LAMP1-positive lysosomes as a result of membrane fusion.
source: As expected, starvation leads to larger LAMP1-positive lysosomes as a result of membrane fusion (Yu et al., 2010) but the localization of C9ORF72 is not altered (Figure 6A, bottom panels).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6A, with membrane fusion mechanism cited from Yu et al., 2010

claim: The localization of C9ORF72 is not altered by starvation.
source: As expected, starvation leads to larger LAMP1-positive lysosomes as a result of membrane fusion (Yu et al., 2010) but the localization of C9ORF72 is not altered (Figure 6A, bottom panels).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6A

claim: 82% of LAMP1-positive lysosomes show C9ORF72 puncta on their periphery in both fed and starved conditions.
source: In fact 82% of LAMP1-positive lysosomes show C9ORF72 puncta on their periphery in both fed and starved conditions (Figure 6B).
evidence: Demonstrated by quantification data shown in Figure 6B

claim: C9ORF72 co-localizes in part with GFP-Rab7a and GFP-Rab9, two small GTPases involved in vesicle trafficking to lysosomes.
source: Consistent with a lysosomal localization, C9ORF72 co-localizes in part with GFP-Rab7a and GFP-Rab9, two small GTPases involved in vesicle trafficking to lysosomes but has little co-localization with GFP-Rab5a or GFP-Rab11a, markers of early and recycling endosomes, respectively (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunofluorescence co-localization data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A, B

claim: C9ORF72 has little co-localization with GFP-Rab5a or GFP-Rab11a, markers of early and recycling endosomes, respectively.
source: Consistent with a lysosomal localization, C9ORF72 co-localizes in part with GFP-Rab7a and GFP-Rab9, two small GTPases involved in vesicle trafficking to lysosomes but has little co-localization with GFP-Rab5a or GFP-Rab11a, markers of early and recycling endosomes, respectively (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunofluorescence co-localization data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A, B

claim: C9ORF72 is enriched on lysosomes by ~3–4 fold in both basal and starved conditions.
source: C9ORF72 is enriched on lysosomes by ~3–4 fold in both basal and starved conditions (Figure 6C).
evidence: Demonstrated by lysosomal immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 6C

claim: C9ORF72 is not enriched after immunoprecipitation of mitochondria.
source: In contrast, C9ORF72 is not enriched after immunoprecipitation of mitochondria (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A) using 3xHA-eGFP-OMP25 as bait (Chen et al., 2016).
evidence: Demonstrated by mitochondrial immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A

claim: A significant pool of C9ORF72 (~85%) is found outside of lysosomes.
source: While C9ORF72 definitively localizes to lysosomes a significant pool of the protein (~85%) is found outside of lysosomes (Figure 6—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Demonstrated by quantification data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2B

claim: ~75% of total C9ORF72 is in the soluble/cytosolic fraction in both RAW264.7 and U2OS cells, whereas 25% is membrane-associated.
source: When we performed a biochemical cytosol/membrane fractionation of RAW264.7 and U2OS cells followed by quantitative immunoblot, we found that ~75% of total C9ORF72 is in the soluble/cytosolic fraction in both cell lines, whereas 25% of total C9ORF72 is membrane-associated (Figure 6—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: Demonstrated by subcellular fractionation data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2C

claim: C9ORF72 distributes to a cytosolic pool and a membrane-bound pool on lysosomes.
source: Thus, the fraction of C9ORF72 not found on lysosomes appears to correspond to a cytosolic pool. In conclusion, C9ORF72 distributes to a cytosolic pool and a membrane-bound pool on lysosomes.
evidence: Based on integration of lysosomal localization and fractionation data

claim: C9ORF72 KO mice age without motor neuron disease.
source: C9ORF72 KO mice age without motor neuron disease (O'Rourke et al., 2016; Jiang et al., 2016; Burberry et al., 2016) but instead develop progressive splenomegaly and lymphadenopathy and ultimately die due to complications of autoimmunity (O'Rourke et al., 2016; Burberry et al., 2016; Atanasio et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to O'Rourke et al., 2016; Jiang et al., 2016; Burberry et al., 2016

claim: C9ORF72 KO mice develop progressive splenomegaly and lymphadenopathy and ultimately die due to complications of autoimmunity.
source: C9ORF72 KO mice age without motor neuron disease (O'Rourke et al., 2016; Jiang et al., 2016; Burberry et al., 2016) but instead develop progressive splenomegaly and lymphadenopathy and ultimately die due to complications of autoimmunity (O'Rourke et al., 2016; Burberry et al., 2016; Atanasio et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to O'Rourke et al., 2016; Burberry et al., 2016; Atanasio et al., 2016

claim: C9ORF72 is expressed at higher levels in bone marrow-derived macrophages from mice than in whole mouse brain or in cultures of rodent neurons.
source: Interestingly, C9ORF72 is expressed at higher levels in bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDM) from mice than in whole mouse brain or in cultures of rodent neurons (Figure 7A).
evidence: Demonstrated by quantitative immunoblot data shown in Figure 7A

claim: Strong expression of C9ORF72 was observed in human monocyte-derived macrophages under traditional M1 polarization conditions and in the presence of TGF-β.
source: Next, we examined human monocyte-derived macrophages (MDMs) under traditional M1 polarization conditions (IFN-γ and LPS treated) or in the presence of TGF-β, which reproduces the homeostatic state of the cells in vitro (Healy et al., 2016) (Figure 7B). We again observed strong expression of C9ORF72 in the macrophage cells.
evidence: Demonstrated by quantitative immunoblot data shown in Figure 7B

claim: In human MDMs, C9ORF72 decorates large organelles that appear to be phagosomes.
source: In human MDMs, C9ORF72 decorates large organelles that appear to be phagosomes (Figure 8A).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 8A

claim: LPS treatment of RAW264.7 cells leads to an ~1.8 fold increase in C9ORF72 protein levels.
source: LPS treatment lead to an ~1.8 fold increase in C9ORF72 protein levels (Figure 8C).
evidence: Demonstrated by quantitative immunoblot data shown in Figure 8C

claim: After a 30 min pulse, F-actin-coated early phagosomes are devoid of LAMP1 and devoid of C9ORF72.
source: After a 30 min pulse (30-0), F-actin-coated early phagosomes are devoid of LAMP1, as expected, and devoid of C9ORF72.
evidence: Demonstrated by pulse-chase immunofluorescence experiment

claim: After a 30 min chase period, late phagosomes lost the majority of their actin coat, are devoid of LAMP1, but started to accumulate C9ORF72.
source: After a 30 min chase period (30-30), late phagosomes lost the majority of their actin coat, are devoid of LAMP1, but started to accumulate C9ORF72.
evidence: Demonstrated by pulse-chase immunofluorescence experiment

claim: After a 90 min chase period, phagolysosomes were devoid of F-actin and accumulated both LAMP1 and C9ORF72.
source: A 90 min chase period (30-90) allowed enough time for late phagosomes to fuse with lysosomes. Phagolysosomes were devoid of F-actin and accumulated both LAMP1 and C9ORF72 (Figure 8D).
evidence: Demonstrated by pulse-chase immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 8D

claim: C9ORF72 starts to accumulate on late-phagosomes once F-actin is being disassembled.
source: Thus, C9ORF72 starts to accumulate on late-phagosomes once F-actin is being disassembled.
evidence: Based on the temporal sequence observed in pulse-chase experiments

claim: C9ORF72 localizes before lysosome fusion on late-phagosomes and remains present on phagolysosomes.
source: C9ORF72 localizes before lysosome fusion on late-phagosomes and remains present on phagolysosomes.
evidence: Based on the temporal sequence observed in pulse-chase experiments

claim: The GeneTex rabbit polyclonal antibody GTX119776 has been used in five published papers.
source: A troubling finding of our study is that the rabbit polyclonal antibody SC-138763, which clearly does not recognize C9ORF72 in any human sample in any application, has been used in 15 published manuscripts to ascribe specific properties to the protein in normal and disease states (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Based on literature search documented in Supplementary file 1

claim: The rabbit polyclonal antibody SC-138763 does not recognize C9ORF72 in any human sample in any application.
source: A troubling finding of our study is that the rabbit polyclonal antibody SC-138763, which clearly does not recognize C9ORF72 in any human sample in any application, has been used in 15 published manuscripts to ascribe specific properties to the protein in normal and disease states (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Based on the validation experiments performed in this study

claim: The rabbit polyclonal antibody SC-138763 has been used in 15 published manuscripts to ascribe specific properties to C9ORF72 in normal and disease states.
source: A troubling finding of our study is that the rabbit polyclonal antibody SC-138763, which clearly does not recognize C9ORF72 in any human sample in any application, has been used in 15 published manuscripts to ascribe specific properties to the protein in normal and disease states (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Based on literature search documented in Supplementary file 1

claim: The 15 papers using SC-138763 have been cited greater than 3000 times.
source: A Google Scholar-based bibliometric approach revealed that those 15 papers have been cited greater than 3000 times and that first layer citations to those citing papers is greater than 66000 citations.
evidence: Based on Google Scholar bibliometric analysis

claim: First layer citations to the 15 papers using SC-138763 is greater than 66000 citations.
source: A Google Scholar-based bibliometric approach revealed that those 15 papers have been cited greater than 3000 times and that first layer citations to those citing papers is greater than 66000 citations.
evidence: Based on Google Scholar bibliometric analysis

claim: PaxDb is a comprehensive proteomic database that provides protein abundance across multiple organisms and tissues/cell lines.
source: We first referenced PaxDb, a comprehensive proteomic database that provides protein abundance across multiple organisms and tissues/cell lines (Wang et al., 2015) (https://pax-db.org/).
evidence: Supported by citation to Wang et al., 2015

claim: The antibody validation strategy developed in this manuscript is easy to implement and scalable.
source: The pipeline is easy to implement and scalable.
evidence: This is a claim made by the authors about their methodology

claim: Application of the antibody validation pipeline to C9ORF72 identified high-quality antibodies revealing C9ORF72 localization to phagosomes/lysosomes.
source: Application to the major ALS disease gene C9ORF72 identified high-quality antibodies revealing C9ORF72 localization to phagosomes/lysosomes.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the experimental results presented

claim: Antibodies that do not recognize C9ORF72 have been used in highly cited papers, raising concern over previously reported C9ORF72 properties.
source: Antibodies that do not recognize C9ORF72 have been used in highly cited papers, raising concern over previously reported C9ORF72 properties.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the validation results and literature analysis

claim: GTX634482 is recommended for immunoblot and immunohistochemical applications on antigen unmasked samples.
source: Thus, we have identified three monoclonal antibodies that effectively and specifically recognize C9ORF72 in multiple applications. The antibody GTX634482 is recommended for immunoblot and immunohistochemical applications on antigen unmasked samples, and GTX632041 is recommended for immunoprecipitation and immunofluorescence.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the validation results

claim: GTX632041 is recommended for immunoprecipitation and immunofluorescence.
source: Thus, we have identified three monoclonal antibodies that effectively and specifically recognize C9ORF72 in multiple applications. The antibody GTX634482 is recommended for immunoblot and immunohistochemical applications on antigen unmasked samples, and GTX632041 is recommended for immunoprecipitation and immunofluorescence.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the validation results

claim: The antibody ab221137 is recommended for immunoblot.
source: The antibody ab221137 is recommended for immunoblot.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the validation results

claim: The performance and specificity of an antibody depends on the nature of the binding to its protein target, including if the recognition involves linear or conformational epitopes.
source: Finally, it is important to mention that all antibodies need to be tested under all conditions since the performance and specificity of an antibody depends on the nature of the binding to its protein target, including if the recognition involves linear or conformational epitopes, which must be determined empirically (Forsström et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Forsström et al., 2015

claim: LRRK2 expression levels are low in the substantia nigra, the most affected area in Parkinson's disease.
source: One example that parallels our findings for C9ORF72 is the major Parkinson disease gene LRRK2 that is broadly expressed in non-neuronal cells, and even within the nervous system, LRRK2 expression levels are low in the most affected area, the substantia nigra (Rui et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Rui et al., 2018

claim: LRRK2 is most highly expressed in immune cells.
source: In fact LRRK2 is most highly expressed in immune cells (Dzamko, 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Dzamko, 2017

claim: 4% PFA followed by Triton X-100 permeabilisation will suffice for the vast majority of targets in immunofluorescence.
source: In a multi-variant screen of fixation conditions for immunofluorescence, it was concluded that 4% PFA followed by Triton X-100 permeabilisation will suffice for the vast majority of targets (Stadler et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Stadler et al., 2010

claim: The antibody validation procedure developed can be applied to any protein target.
source: The process we outline can be applied to any protein target and here it led us to the recognition of problems with the C9ORF72 literature and to the discovery of unexpected properties of the protein.
evidence: This is a claim about the generalizability of the method

claim: Individual steps of the antibody validation pipeline can be used in isolation depending on the needs of the user.
source: While we applied the pipeline to all known commercial antibodies against C9ORF72, the process is certainly applicable to home-made antibodies and individual steps of the pipeline can be used in isolation depending on the needs of the user.
evidence: This is a statement about the flexibility of the method
